images.title: The L gives the LCM
images.purpose: Show that multiplying the divisors by the last row of the ladder for 630 and 770 gives the LCM.
images.composition: One ladder in the centre left with four rows, an L shaped highlight along the divisor column and the bottom row, and one result line on the right.
exact_structure: Row 1: 630 and 770. Row 2: 315 and 385. Row 3: 63 and 77. Row 4: 9 and 11. Exactly 4 rows, 8 numbers.
Exactly 3 divisors in a column to the left of rows 1 to 3, top to bottom: 2, 5, 7, in teal #0072B2.
Thin grey #6B7280 division bars: one vertical bar right of the divisor column and one horizontal line under each of rows 1 to 3.
One reddish purple #CC79A7 L shaped band: down the divisor column 2, 5, 7 and along the bottom row 9 and 11, with 9 and 11 in amber #E69F00.
To the right, one bold line: LCM = 2 × 5 × 7 × 9 × 11 = 6930.
rejection: any row that is not the row above divided by its divisor
the L shaped band missing either the divisors or the bottom row 9 and 11
images.takeaway: The divisors times the last row give the LCM: it holds both numbers with nothing extra.
images.description: A division ladder for 630 and 770 ending in 9 and 11, with an L shape around 2, 5, 7 and 9, 11, and LCM = 6930.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video on getting the LCM from the same ladder.
images.teaching_notes: Trace the L from top to bottom and then along the last row; every number on it is multiplied.

image_decisions.why: The L shape on the ladder is the visual rule students need to remember for the LCM.
